headline: FREEGOLD DRILLS 336.8m AT 1.32 g/t AU FROM SURFACE — 6-RIG ALASKA PROGRAM CLOSES ON GOLDEN SUMMIT PREFEASIBILITY
source_name: North of 60 Mining News / Freegold Ventures Limited (TSX: FVL)
snippet: Freegold Ventures Limited (TSX: FVL) released June 17, 2026 new infill drill results from its Golden Summit Gold Project in Alaska — led by hole GS2562 which returned 336.8 metres grading 1.32 g/t Au from only 26.5 metres depth, including a higher-grade core of 36 metres at 2.37 g/t Au from 75.3 metres and 96 metres at 1.63 g/t Au from 119.5 metres. Six rigs are currently operating as part of a large-scale 2026 program targeting an updated mineral resource estimate and the 2027 Pre-Feasibility Study, with the principal objective of increasing confidence in the higher-grade zones and identifying starter-pit geometry. At gold holding near $4,300 per ounce — still historically profitable for low-strip open-pit production — a 336-metre infill intercept commencing less than 27 metres from surface, at grades 40% above the project's resource average, directly de-risks the PFS cost model and supports the thesis that Golden Summit's high-grade corridors can anchor an attractive initial mining case.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER ENTERS GDX TODAY — MOROCCO SILVER MINER JOINS WORLD'S MOST TRACKED MINING ETF AT CLOSE
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Aya Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX: AYA; NASDAQ: AYA)
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX: AYA; NASDAQ: AYA) is added to the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) effective at the close of trading June 19, 2026, following GDX's quarterly rebalance — making Aya shares mandatory holdings for any fund benchmarking against the ETF, which manages more than $15 billion in assets. The milestone follows record Q1-2026 financial results driven by the expanded Zgounder silver mine in Morocco and ongoing advancement of the Boumadine polymetallic project. GDX inclusion triggers forced-buying from passive funds indexed to the benchmark and structurally expands the company's institutional investor base — historically one of the most durable short-to-medium-term positive liquidity catalysts available to a mid-tier precious metals producer. For investors watching gold and silver miners during a 25% correction from the January ATH, Aya's promotion from benchmark-adjacent to benchmark-included is a concrete institutional validation that brings new buyers into the register at current prices.

headline: LUMINA METALS LISTS ON WARSAW — 9MT COPPER, 900MOZ SILVER PORPHYRY COURTS KGHM AND EUROPEAN CAPITAL
snippet: Lumina Metals Corp. (TSX: LMCU) commenced dual trading on the Warsaw Stock Exchange on June 16, 2026 while maintaining its TSX listing — a strategic move to bring the company's flagship Nowa Sól copper-silver porphyry in southwest Poland onto KGHM's home exchange. Nowa Sól contains an estimated 9 million tonnes of copper and 900 million ounces of silver, one of the largest undeveloped copper-silver deposits in Europe. The listing follows a letter of intent signed with KGHM Polska Miedź S.A. — one of the world's largest integrated copper-silver producers, which operates adjacent Kupferschiefer belt assets — and the commencement of a NI 43-101 pre-feasibility study in May 2026, after a C$406 million TSX IPO in April. The Warsaw listing opens Lumina to institutional capital pools that already understand Polish copper geology and KGHM's strategic optionality — a key investor relations step for a project of this scale to reach its potential development value in the current copper-scarcity narrative.

headline: OROCO CONFIRMS SANTO TOMÁS BLOCK MODEL — 48.6m AT 0.56% CU IN PHASE 2 SOUTH ZONE INFILL
snippet: Oroco Resource Corp. (TSXV: OCO) reported June 18, 2026 the second set of assay results from its Phase 2 resource drilling program at the South Zone of its Santo Tomás copper porphyry in Choix, Sinaloa, Mexico — with hole S026 returning 48.6 metres at 0.56% Cu (0.67% CuEq) plus two additional intervals of 59 metres at 0.20% Cu and 23.45 metres at 0.16% Cu, all consistent with the block model in the project's 2024 Technical Report. Earlier Phase 2 holes intersected 228 metres at 0.49% CuEq and 212 metres at 0.44% CuEq — confirming the broad, continuous nature of the near-surface, low-strip porphyry system at economic copper grades. With COMEX copper at approximately $5.89/lb ahead of the June 30 US refined copper tariff deadline, a Sinaloa porphyry advancing Phase 2 infill drilling toward a resource update keeps OCO on the catalyst calendar for investors building copper development exposure across the North American supply chain.

headline: JUNE 30 COPPER TARIFF COUNTDOWN: COMMERCE SECRETARY DEADLINE FORCES REFINED IMPORT DECISION — COMEX PREMIUM REBUILDS
snippet: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces a June 30, 2026 statutory deadline to deliver a formal Section 232 assessment to President Trump on whether phased tariffs of 15% (from January 2027) and 30% (from January 2028) on refined copper imports are warranted — a decision that, if implemented, would structurally advantage North American copper miners over imported refined metal. US copper imports more than doubled year-on-year to 533,000 tonnes in Q1 2026 as buyers pre-empt anticipated tariffs, and the COMEX–LME spread has re-widened to approximately $400 per tonne in early June — far below the $2,937/t peak of July 2025 but rebuilding steadily as the deadline approaches. The market is pricing the most likely outcome as a 15% phased tariff rather than a sweeping immediate duty, keeping copper near $5.89/lb COMEX. For investors holding North American copper developers in BC porphyry corridors, Arizona, or the Bathurst VMS camp, the June 30 ruling creates a near-term binary catalyst that could redefine domestic copper's premium to LME for the next several years.

headline: MINRES BALD HILL BACK ONLINE — 18-MONTH LITHIUM HALT ENDS AS SPODUMENE TOPS $2,000/T, PRODUCTION DUE JULY
source_name: Mining Technology / Mineral Resources Ltd. (ASX: MIN)
snippet: Mineral Resources Ltd. (ASX: MIN) formally restarted crushing circuits at its Bald Hill Lithium Mine in Western Australia in June 2026 — ending an 18-month care-and-maintenance period that began in November 2024 when sustained lithium price deterioration rendered operations uneconomic. The dual-stream operation 50 kilometres south-east of Kambalda targets 165,000 dry metric tonnes per year of 5.1% Li₂O spodumene concentrate, with first production guided to July 2026 at a restart capital cost of approximately A$20 million. The revival comes as spodumene prices climbed above US$2,000 per tonne for the first time since late 2023, driven by Australian production curtailments, Zimbabwe's raw mineral export ban, and Chinese EV infrastructure commitments — with battery-grade lithium carbonate up more than 125% from its June 2025 trough. Bald Hill's restart is the first concrete production resumption among Australia's mothballed spodumene operations in the current price recovery, a data point that validates improving sector economics for investors holding lithium developer and producer exposure.

headline: F3 URANIUM LAUNCHES ATHABASCA SUMMER PROGRAM — TARGETS NEW DISCOVERIES BEYOND TETRA ZONE AT PATTERSON LAKE NORTH
source_name: Investing News Network / F3 Uranium Corp. (TSXV: FUU)
snippet: F3 Uranium Corp. (TSXV: FUU) announced June 16, 2026 the launch of its 2026 summer exploration program across the Patterson Lake North Project in the Western Athabasca Basin — the same south-western Basin margin hosting Paladin Energy's Triple R deposit and NexGen Energy's Arrow deposit. The program advances new target areas across three PLN properties — Patterson Lake North, Minto, and Broach — while 3D-DCIP and resistivity geophysical surveys run directly over the Tetra Zone to define the next drill targets. Four high-priority Patterson West conductors that exhibit geophysical signatures similar to the Tetra Zone are prioritised for drill testing, expanding F3's discovery surface well beyond its known zones on one of the largest single-explorer land packages along the prospective Basin margin. With uranium spot near $86/lb and US utilities contracting ahead of the 2028 Russian-import ban, a Western Athabasca Basin junior with PLN-scale acreage and multiple geophysically defined undrilled targets is positioned for a discovery catalyst in the summer drill window.

headline: BRIXTON METALS DRILLS ONTARIO SILVER TAILINGS FOR MAIDEN MRE — LANGIS CAMP CONVERTS HISTORIC RESIDUE TO RESOURCE
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation (TSXV: BBB) announced June 18, 2026 the commencement of a dedicated sonic-drilling campaign designed to produce a maiden NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate from the historic tailings at its Langis Silver Project in Ontario's Cobalt silver mining district — the most celebrated historic silver camp in Canada. Sonic drilling provides continuous core-like samples from unconsolidated tailings material, enabling higher resource classification confidence than conventional RC methods and reducing the sample interval needed to support NI 43-101 block modelling. At silver near $67/oz — 45% below the January 28 all-time high — the conversion of a historically documented tailings body into a compliant resource estimate is a low-risk, low-capital pathway to adding silver ounces to a project portfolio without greenfield geological uncertainty. For Ontario silver investors, the commencement milestone marks the transition from a sampling-stage tailings target to a resource-classified asset that can be appraised on a per-ounce basis and included in net asset value calculations.

headline: ASM SHAREHOLDERS VOTE JUNE 22 ON ENERGY FUELS' $299M RARE EARTHS SCHEME — WOULD CREATE LARGEST EX-CHINA REE PLATFORM
snippet: Australian Strategic Materials Ltd. (ASX: ASM) shareholders vote in Perth on June 22, 2026 on a scheme of arrangement under which Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU; TSX: EFR) will acquire 100% of ASM for approximately US$299 million — with ASM holders receiving 0.053 Energy Fuels shares or CDIs plus up to A$0.13 cash per share, representing A$1.60 total. If approved, the combined entity will merge Energy Fuels' NdPr oxide separation at White Mesa Mill — now supported by a conditional US$725 million Pentagon loan — with ASM's operating Korean Metals Plant and its planned US rare earth alloy facility, creating the world's largest fully integrated rare earth mine-to-metal producer outside China. The combined platform would span the full supply chain from mining and uranium processing through oxide separation, metal reduction, and final alloy output — precisely the ex-China REE chain that US and European defence procurement has been seeking to establish. ASM's board unanimously recommends shareholders vote in favour in the absence of a superior proposal.

headline: GOLD DOWN 25% FROM ATH — GOLDSILVER.COM DISSECTS CPI, FED AMBIGUITY, AND IRAN DEAL FOR WHAT COMES NEXT
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 2026 gold price analysis examines the three forces behind gold's 25% correction from its January 28 all-time high of $5,589 to the current $4,200-$4,300 range: energy-led CPI upside that sustained the FOMC's hawkish dot chart, Fed Chair Warsh's deliberate non-submission of his personal dot leaving his policy stance ambiguous, and the risk-on relief from the US-Iran Strait of Hormuz interim agreement that pulled oil lower and trimmed the immediate inflation case for another hike. The piece argues that lower oil from Hormuz reopening is structurally bullish for gold because it removes the most immediate inflationary pressure suppressing the metal since February — setting the stage for a renewed bull leg once Q3 CPI data confirms energy deflation. With most major institutional gold price forecasts for year-end 2026 still in the $5,400-$6,300 range, the current correction represents the deepest pullback of the 2024-2026 bull cycle — and historically, the deepest correction within a confirmed bull run has preceded the cycle's largest subsequent advance.
